inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted average, Q3-2026 10-Q EPS note (167.4m; basic outstanding 165.5m at 3 Oct 2026). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. The Silvus share-settled earnout (up to $600m, fair value $214m) is not in the diluted count until earned, so it is deducted in the equity bridge at fair value instead.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 3 Oct 2026 = FY2025 cash-flow add-back $293m + 9M-2026 $307m - 9M-2025 $213m (Q3-2026 10-Q cash flow statement and Note 9). MSI publishes no combined figure and no separate equity-award withholding-tax line ('Issuances of common stock, net of tax' is a net +$45m inflow in 9M-2026), so the cash-flow add-back is the basis.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.3% (10-year UST) + ~4.75% ERP x beta ~0.9 = cost of equity ~8.6%; pre-tax debt cost ~5.0-5.6% (Aug-2026 issues at 4.85%/5.65%), ~3.9% after tax, on ~10% of capital -> ~8.1%, rounded up to 8.5% for 2.3x net leverage and serial-acquirer integration risk. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged once, through the scenario weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (liability ~$0.5bn incl. current) left inside EBITDA as rent expense under US GAAP; not added to net debt. One treatment only.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is immaterial ($17m book, ~$5m/yr earnings); deducted in the equity bridge at ~15x earnings.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route (US operating company; dcf-methods routing row 1; no adaptations file needed). Fresh build, no prior DCF and no memory entry. FY0 is the trailing twelve months to 3 Oct 2026 (revenue 12,603 = FY2025 11,682 + 9M-26 9,223 - 9M-25 8,302), so 'year 1' is the next twelve months and end-of-year discounting is honest for a mid-November valuation date. last_fcf 2,147 = TTM reported FCF 2,534 (OCF 2,838 less capex 304) less TTM SBC 387; it is a LEVERED figure (after ~$440m of cash interest) while the engine projects unlevered FCF, so year-1 projected FCF (~2.9bn) is not directly comparable: add back ~$340m after-tax interest and the abnormal ~$730m 9M-2026 inventory/receivables build. Interest income (TTM ~$30m) is NOT stripped: the company is in net debt, so there is no cash pile to double-count. EBITDA anchor: TTM operating earnings + D&A = 3,639; + SBC 387 + non-cash Silvus earnout charges 178 - Hytera litigation gains 136 = ~4,068, 32.3% of revenue pre-SBC. Acquisition transaction fees are left in as a recurring cost of a serial acquirer. Buybacks: TTM $1,033m (FY2025 1,154 + 9M-26 543 - 9M-25 664) against SBC of $387m, so the flat count is funded more than twice over (count has fallen 169.0m -> 167.4m diluted YoY). Pending: C$675m purchase of Bell Mobility's LMR network-services business (expected H1-2027) is not in debt or revenue; treated as value-neutral at cost. Strategic investments of $292m (at cost, incl. BRINC) are excluded from the bridge as conservative. Analysis JSON was not yet present at build time; scenario axes are drawn from the 10-K/10-Q. No FY2026 guidance paragraph exists in the extracted filings (guidance lives in the 8-K press release, not fetched), so year-1 growth rests on Q3-2026 run-rate: +12% reported, of which $211m (7pts) acquired, ~5% organic.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue CAGR less acquired growth (organic ~5-7%); equity CAGR unusable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is not meaningful: stockholders' equity was negative from FY2015 to FY2021 (-$558m in FY2020, +$131m FY2022, +$2,427m FY2025) because of buybacks and pension AOCI. Growth selection falls back to revenue. EPS and FCF CAGRs (12-18%) run well ahead of revenue (9%) on margin expansion and buybacks, which cannot compound indefinitely.
historical_growth.notes: FY2020/FY2022 -> FY2025, calendar fiscal years. FCF CAGRs are on owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC; no interest-income strip because MSI has been in net debt throughout): 1,267 -> 1,395 -> 2,279. Owner-FCF 5-year CAGR (12.5%) is slightly below reported (13.0%): SBC has risen from 1.7% to 2.5% of revenue (3.1% TTM after Silvus/D-Fend retention awards), so a growing share of reported FCF growth is being paid for in stock. Revenue CAGRs include acquisitions (Silvus added ~4pts in the trailing year).

base.rationale: Growth: ~5.5% organic plus ~1.5pts of D-Fend/tuck-in carry in the next twelve months, then mid-single digits fading to 3%. Margin: 32.3% TTM pre-SBC (ex Hytera gains and earnout charges) rising ~35bp/yr on Software & Services mix (S&S segment margin ~27-28% GAAP and climbing) to 35%. SBC: 3.07% TTM, elevated by acquisition retention awards, easing to 2.6% (FY2025 was 2.5%). D&A: 4.6% TTM, falling as Silvus intangibles amortise (lower D&A raises cash tax; conservative). Capex 2.4% = TTM. Tax 23% = TTM effective and cash rate. Working capital: mild consumer of cash on growth (receivables + contract assets + inventory slightly exceed payables + contract liabilities).

scenario_narratives.base: The LMR franchise keeps doing what it has done for a decade: public-safety agencies refresh radios and infrastructure on long cycles (APX NEXT, P25 upgrades), the $15.7bn backlog (of which $11.9bn is multi-year Software & Services) converts on schedule, and Video and Command Center grow high-single to low-double digits. Silvus MANET and D-Fend counter-drone earn their purchase prices but not much more. Organic growth runs 5-6% for five years and fades to 3%; mix shift toward recurring software and services lifts pre-SBC EBITDA margin from ~32% to 35%. Leverage (2.3x net debt/EBITDA) is worked down from cash flow while tuck-in M&A continues at a pace the flows can fund.
scenario_narratives.bull: Defence and border-security demand makes Silvus and D-Fend genuine second growth engines (MANET radios for unmanned systems, counter-UAS for airports, stadiums and public safety), International keeps growing in the high teens as it did in 2026, and AI features (Assist, agentic 911 call handling, video analytics) raise software attach and pricing across the installed base. Cloud migration of Command Center and video compounds recurring revenue; organic growth holds 7-9% for five years and margins reach 38% as Software & Services passes 40% of sales. This needs the acquired defence businesses, the public-safety AI upsell and the international push all to work, on top of an undisturbed LMR core.
scenario_narratives.bear: State and local budgets tighten as federal grant funding (the indirect payer for much US public-safety capex) is cut, stretching radio refresh cycles; broadband push-to-talk over FirstNet and LTE/5G starts to substitute for LMR devices at the margin, most visibly in the commercial PCR channel; the UK Airwave/ESN revenue stream steps down under the CMA price cap and eventual ESN transition; Video stays a commoditising hardware fight with Axon and low-cost camera vendors; and Silvus misses its earnout targets as defence orders prove lumpy. Tariff and supply-chain costs (the 2026 inventory build is $0.5bn) are not fully passed through. Growth falls to 2-4%, margins slip to 31%, SBC stays at 3% as retention awards recur with each deal.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): the balance sheet is investment grade and the downside is slower refresh and margin drift, not solvency, but net debt has gone from ~$4bn to $9.3bn in fifteen months to buy two defence-adjacent businesses at high multiples, and US public-safety demand depends on government budgets. Base 50%: a decade of mid-single-digit organic growth with steady margin expansion, backed by a $15.7bn backlog, is the modal outcome. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): it requires three independent things to go right at once: defence/C-UAS scaling, AI software monetisation and sustained high-teens international growth.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Motorola Solutions is a high-quality, low-volatility franchise: dominant share in mission-critical LMR, sticky government customers, a large multi-year backlog and a record of converting ~100% of earnings to cash. The house model charges SBC as a real cost, discounts unlevered owner FCF at 8.5%, caps the terminal multiple at 20x and deducts $9.3bn of net debt plus pension and earnout claims. On that basis the business is worth materially less than the market price, which capitalises unlevered owner FCF at roughly 34x: the market is paying for more than the bull path, with an exit multiple above the 20x cap. The valuation is a statement about price, not about business quality.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value is 62% of base enterprise value, so the result is sensitive to WACC; but with the 20x terminal cap binding, even a 6.5% WACC only lifts the base case to about $399/share. No cell of the sensitivity grid reaches the market price: the price needs both the bull driver path and an exit multiple above 20x.

Acquisition accounting: Silvus ($4.4bn) and D-Fend ($1.3bn) revenue and margin are not separately disclosed; if they grow well above the group rate the base growth path is too low, if they miss the earnout targets the bear path applies.
No FY2026/FY2027 management guidance was available in the extracted filings; year-1 growth is a run-rate judgment and should be re-anchored to the Q4-2026 earnings release.
Hytera litigation recoveries ($157m in FY2025, $73m in 9M-2026) are excluded from the margin base; further recoveries are upside not modelled.

The 9M-2026 inventory build (+$503m) is treated as temporary; if it reflects structurally higher working-capital intensity (tariff buffering, defence hardware), the -5% working-capital capture is too generous.
Pending C$675m Bell Mobility LMR-services acquisition (H1-2027) will add debt and revenue not in this model.
